description: We’re professional web developers and software engineering students building tech for real-world impact. With collective experience in full-stack development, AI/ML, and data visualization, we specialize in turning complex data into practical platforms. Our goal is to bridge satellite science and software engineering to build an accessible wildfire monitoring solution that turns NASA data into clear, real-time insights.
summary: UniFire is a web app that turns 25 years of NASA fire data into one honest record . NASA's MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) satellites see fire differently. VIIRS's sharper pixels catch small fires MODIS misses, so merging them raw makes fire look 6× higher when it actually fell about 30%. Our algorithm, learns month by month how the two satellites differ from the years both flew, then converts the older record, with error ranges. In a blind test it predicts a hidden year within 6.5%. Pick any area and UniFire shows a harmonized fire map, a 25-year burning calendar, and a Fire Activity Score from Safe to Critical. It gives researchers, journalists and local agencies a trustworthy view of fires the world rarely sees.
details: UniFire is a web app that harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS active fire records into one consistent fire radiative power baseline and shows it as a burning activity calendar. Users pick an area of interest and see 2000 to 2026 burning activity as a 12-month calendar colored against the area’s average, plus an annual anomaly timeline and a time-lapse. Adjustable corrections for footprint size, detection sensitivity and overpass time put both sensors on one scale. It helps emergency responders, land managers and scientists see when burning is normal or unusual. The prototype runs on synthetic records with the same structure as real data; the pipeline is designed to switch to live NASA FIRMS data.
